sections.title: Multi-run Architecture & Concept
sections.content:
Modern applications frequently consist of distributed services that must execute concurrently (e.g. Backend API + Frontend + Background Worker). Starting each runtime manually is inefficient.

The Multi-run module allows you to define declarative 'Process Groups'. A single click on the Play button launches the entire container stack simultaneously, with each service running in a fully isolated, monitored process tree.

sections.title: Creating & Populating Process Groups
sections.content:
Navigate to the Master Manager window and select the 'Multi-run' tab:

  1. Create Group: Click + in the left sidebar and specify a group identifier (e.g. 'FullStack Dev').
  2. Select Members: The middle tree lists all scanned projects and their environments. Check any environment box to assign it to the active group.
  3. Save: Assigned members appear in the right matrix. Click Save Group Changes to persist group definitions to configuration.

sections.title: Execution Order & Scripts (3-Zone Drag & Drop)
sections.content:
Fine-tune container execution within the 'Group Members' matrix:

Advanced 3-Zone Drag & Drop Reordering

Row order defines execution sequence (e.g. starting a database before an API gateway). The table utilizes an intelligent 3-zone drop target system:

  • Insert: Dropping onto the top or bottom edge of a target row inserts the dragged row before or after it.
  • Swap: Dropping directly into the center of a target row swaps positions between the two entries.

Script Override per Container

By default, members execute their primary default script. To run an alternate entry point for a specific container group (e.g. worker.py), simply double-click the Script cell to override it.

Persistence: Click Save Group Changes after any reordering or script modification.

sections.title: Execution Lifecycle & Smart Respawn
sections.content:
Launch a container group by setting the Mini-Bar to M (Multi) mode, selecting the group, and clicking Play ▶.

Concurrency & Collision Protection

VenvHub Pro prevents duplicate executions. If any project in the group is already running, startup halts and alerts the developer to prevent socket and port collisions.

Smart Respawn Engine

If a single microservice within an active group crashes while other services remain healthy:

  1. Fix the defect in your codebase.
  2. Click Play ▶ on the Mini-Bar toolbar again.

The Smart Respawn engine evaluates running states:

  • Inspects the group matrix.
  • Identifies healthy active services -> SKIPPED (Undisturbed).
  • Identifies the crashed service -> RESPAWNED (Relaunched).

There is no need to restart the entire stack—only crashed processes are selectively revived.

sections.title: Process Ownership & Group Isolation
sections.content:
VenvHub Pro enforces a robust process ownership model. When launching a group named 'MyAPI', every spawned PID registers an ownership tag binding it to that specific group context.

Why Process Ownership Matters:

Consider overlapping group configurations:

  • Group A: contains Project 1 and Project 2.
  • Group B: contains Project 2 and Project 3.

If Group A is running and you issue a Stop command to Group B, standard PID killing might accidentally terminate Project 2. Process ownership prevents this cross-group interference.

Isolation Guarantee: Clicking Stop ■ terminates strictly and exclusively processes launched under that specific group banner, leaving other concurrent runtimes untouched.

sections.title: Windows Low-Level Stability (Job Objects & Handles)
sections.content:
VenvHub Pro includes low-level Windows process management using native C-runtime bindings via ctypes:

1. Orphan Process Elimination (Windows Job Objects)

Upon initialization, child processes assign to a native Windows Job Object with the JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE attribute.

  • If VenvHub Pro exits or crashes unexpectedly, the Windows kernel intercepts the Job closure and instantly terminates all associated subprocesses.
  • Prevents orphaned background processes from locking listening ports or consuming RAM.

2. PID Collision Protection (Windows Process Handles)

Windows aggressively recycles Process IDs (PIDs). If a monitored PID terminates and Windows assigns the same ID to another system application, registry polling could misidentify processes.

  • VenvHub Pro retains an open kernel-level Process Handle throughout process lifecycle.
  • An open handle prevents Windows from recycling that specific PID until VenvHub explicitly closes the handle.
  • Guarantees zero risk of accidental termination of external system processes.
Thread-Safe Resource Management: All kernel handles are protected by thread locks and close cleanly during normal termination, preventing handle leaks.
